record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: Do the observed redshifts of galaxies and quasars necessarily imply that the universe is expanding, or can a physically and observationally supported non-cosmological redshift mechanism, such as gravitational redshift, tired light, variable mass, chronometric cosmology, or multiple scattering, explain those redshifts without producing unacceptable image blurring, frequency dependence, or conflicts with intergalactic-medium constraints?

evidence.quote: Some observations will be discussed or rediscussed in order to show that these facts were not strictly proven. The possibility of alternative hypotheses different from the Big Bang theory is still open.

All these proposed mechanisms show us that it is quite possible to construct a scenario with non-cosmological redshifts. Nonetheless, all these theories are at present just speculations without direct experimental or observational support.

artifact.status_search_result: Multiple independent observations strongly disfavor non-cosmological redshift mechanisms. The CMB FIRAS blackbody spectrum constrains any tired-light-style mechanism by many standard deviations; Type Ia supernova light-curve and spectral time-dilation measurements (including the Dark Energy Survey program out to z~1) confirm the expected (1+z) factor and rule out non-time-dilating cosmologies; Tolman surface-brightness tests further support expansion. Image-sharpness and frequency-independence constraints rule out scattering-based mechanisms. The community consensus, supported by these tests, is that no proposed non-cosmological redshift mechanism satisfies all the observational constraints simultaneously.

status_evidence.title: Errors in Tired Light Cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: FIRAS data limits any (1+z)^3 blackbody prefactor to 1.00001±0.00005; tired-light fails by ~100,000 standard deviations.
status_evidence.claim: Tired-light is ruled out by CMB spectrum and supernova time dilation.

status_evidence.title: Dark Energy Survey Supernova Program: cosmological time dilation out to z~1
status_evidence.snippet: A large Type Ia supernova sample provides the most precise measurement of cosmological time dilation to date, ruling out non-time-dilating cosmological models at high significance.
status_evidence.claim: Supernova time dilation confirms expansion and disfavors static/tired-light models.

status_evidence.title: Tolman Surface Brightness Test IV
status_evidence.snippet: Tolman surface brightness measurements support reality of cosmological expansion.
status_evidence.claim: Surface-brightness scaling consistent with expansion, not tired light.

status_evidence.title: Tired light - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Tired-light models are inconsistent with observed time dilation, CMB blackbody, and image sharpness of distant objects.
status_evidence.claim: Non-cosmological redshift proposals are observationally excluded.
